title: esptool 5.6.0 loader.py: reset strategy for the USB-Serial/JTAG PID
note: Line 850: 'if mode == "usb-reset" or self.get_usb_vid_pid()[1] == self.USB_JTAG_SERIAL_PID: return (USBJTAGSerialReset(self._port),)' - esptool resets 303a:1001 boards into the bootloader over USB.

title: espressif/esp-usb esp_tinyusb usb_descriptors.c: default PID of the TinyUSB device stack
note: Lines 20-22: '#define USB_TUSB_PID (0x4000 | _PID_MAP(CDC, 0) | _PID_MAP(MSC, 1) | _PID_MAP(HID, 2) | _PID_MAP(MIDI, 3) | _PID_MAP(AUDIO, 4) | _PID_MAP(VENDOR, 5) | _PID_MAP(MTP, 6) )', used with the Espressif VID (lines 46-53). One CDC interface only gives 303a:4001; the range 0x4000-0x407f is this default scheme. The application, not the ROM, owns such a USB device.

title: Observed on a test board: ESP32-S3 running firmware with its own TinyUSB CDC stack (303a:4001)
note: observed, not a published source. A fresh ESP32-S3 enumerated as 303a:4001; 'esptool --before default-reset --after hard-reset flash-id' failed with 'Failed to connect to Espressif device: No serial data received.'; a 1200-bps touch did not restart it. Treated as: no automatic reset into the bootloader on usb_cdc_app ports.

title: esptool documentation: Boot Mode Selection (ESP32-S3)
note: 'The ESP32-S3 will enter the serial bootloader when GPIO0 is held low on reset.' 'Many boards use a button marked "Flash" (or "BOOT" on some Espressif development boards) that pulls GPIO0 low when pressed.' DTR/RTS are active low; 'if both RTS and DTR are asserted together, this doesn't reset the chip'.

title: PlatformIO Core 6.2.0 builder/tools/piointegration.py: extra.flash_images of pio project metadata
note: '"extra": dict(flash_images=[{"offset": item[0], "path": globalenv.subst(item[1])} for item in globalenv.get("FLASH_EXTRA_IMAGES", [])])', then IDE_EXTRA_DATA/INTEGRATION_EXTRA_DATA are merged in; platform-espressif32 v6.9.0 builder/frameworks/arduino.py line 39 adds application_offset ($ESP32_APP_OFFSET). Observed offline 2026-11-07 (6.9.0 and 8.0.0, Arduino): bootloader.bin at 0x1000 (ESP32) or 0x0000 (S3, C6), partitions.bin 0x8000, boot_app0.bin 0xe000, application_offset 0x10000.

title: platform-espressif32 v6.9.0 builder/main.py: esptool upload command and nobuild
note: Upload (esptool protocol): '--chip', mcu, '--port', '--baud', '--before', '--after', 'write_flash', '-z', '--flash_mode', '${__get_board_flash_mode(__env__)}', '--flash_freq', '${__get_board_f_image(__env__)}', '--flash_size', board.get('upload.flash_size', 'detect') ... $ESP32_APP_OFFSET $SOURCE; then 'for image in env.get("FLASH_EXTRA_IMAGES", []): env.Append(UPLOADERFLAGS=[image[0], env.subst(image[1])])' (lines 445-463). elf2image uses the same --flash_mode/--flash_freq (lines 319-322). Lines 360-381: with 'nobuild' BuildProgram() is not called, so the framework script that sets FLASH_EXTRA_IMAGES does not run and only the app is uploaded (observed on a test board, 2026-11-07).

title: esptool v5.6.0: write-flash, image-info and the chip check
note: write-flash takes <address> <filename> pairs and --flash-mode [keep|qio|qout|dio|dout], --flash-freq, --flash-size [detect|keep|...], -z/--compress (esptool write-flash --help, v5.6.0). image-info prints 'Detected image type: ESP32-S3', 'Flash freq: 80m', 'Flash mode: DIO' (observed 2026-11-07). loader.py connect: 'raise FatalError(f"This chip is {chip_type}, not {self.CHIP_NAME}. Wrong chip argument?")' before anything is written.

title: Observed on a test board: WT32-ETH01 V1.4 after an app-only upload (2026-11-07)
note: observed, not a published source. pio run -t nobuild -t upload wrote 769472 bytes at 0x00010000 only; the factory partition table of the WT32 has its factory app at 0x20000, so the bootloader reported 'image at 0x20000 has invalid magic byte' and 'No bootable app partitions in the partition table' in a reboot loop. Board-observed; the flash must write bootloader, partition table and boot_app0 with the app.

note: observed offline on PlatformIO Core 6.2.0 + espressif32 6.9.0: top-level object keyed by env name with build_type, cc_flags, cc_path, compiler_type, cxx_flags, cxx_path, defines, env_name, extra, gdb_path, includes, libsource_dirs, prog_path, svd_path, targets. prog_path is the ELF; there is no toolchain field, the prefix is cc_path without 'gcc'.
